item.title: About
item.description:
Patch Dispatch publishes short write-ups of security vulnerabilities in Windows, Linux, PHP and npm: what is affected, how serious it is and how to fix it.

How a dispatch is made

  1. A collector reads official sources: the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, NVD, OSV, the GitHub Advisory Database, the Microsoft Security Response Center and the Debian and Ubuntu security trackers.
  2. An AI agent picks the few vulnerabilities each day that are worth a post.
  3. A second agent writes the post from the official data.
  4. A third agent checks every claim against the original advisory and sends the draft back when something doesn’t match.
  5. A person reads the final version and approves it before it goes out.

The pipeline is still being built. Until it runs, posts are written by hand while each step is tested.

item.title: Corrections
item.description:
Mistakes are possible. When one is found, the post gets a dated correction note at the top that says what was wrong and what changed. Posts are never quietly edited.

To report a mistake, email corrections@patchdispatch.dev with the post’s address and what you think is wrong. A link to the official source that shows it helps most.

Corrections so far

None yet.

item.title: Disclaimer
item.description:
Posts on this site are generated by AI agents from public vulnerability data (NVD, CISA KEV, OSV, the GitHub Advisory Database and vendor advisories) and checked by a person before publishing.

They can still contain errors, miss details or go out of date as advisories change. They are provided for information only and are not security, legal or professional advice.

Before you act on a post, confirm the details in the original advisory linked at the end of it and make your own assessment for your systems.
